title: st.dialog Does Not Close Immediately After User Action if Followed by Blocking Operation (e.g. time.sleep(15))
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.dialog` to collect feedback from a user, if the feedback submission is followed by a blocking operation (e.g., `time.sleep(15)`), the dialog's title remains visible on the screen until the blocking operation is complete. This creates a poor user experience because the user may expect the dialog to disappear immediately after submitting their input, but the dialog remains visible until the blocking operation finishes.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st

[USER].dialog("Cast your vote")
def vote(item):
    st.write(f"Why is {item} your favorite?")
    reason = st.text_input("Because...")
    if st.button("Submit"):
        st.session_state.vote = {"item": item, "reason": reason}
        st.rerun()

if "vote" not in st.session_state:
    st.write("Vote for your favorite")

    if st.button("A"):
        vote("A")
    if st.button("B"):
        vote("B")
else:
    time.sleep(15)
    f"You voted for {st.session_state.vote['item']} because {st.session_state.vote['reason']}"
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use the provided code below to mimic collecting user feedback using `st.dialog`.
2. After the user submits their feedback, the code simulates a blocking operation using `time.sleep(15)`.
3. Notice that the dialog's title ("Cast your vote") remains visible for the full 15 seconds while `time.sleep(15)` is running.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog should close immediately after the user submits their input, regardless of any blocking operation that follows, so that the UI responds promptly to the user's action.

### Current Behavior

The dialog remains open until the blocking operation (`time.sleep(15)`) is completed. This means the title "Cast your vote" is displayed on the screen for 15 seconds.

![2024-09-04_21-39-12 (1)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f664f9f7-24cf-4b3b-8fad-d5fdcf0dcfdb)


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.37.1
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: Mac OS / Linux Ubuntu 
- Browser: Chrome 


### Additional Information

### GIF:
_Attach a GIF that shows the issue occurring._

### Additional Context:

I plan to use `st.dialog` to collect user confirmation before running a long operation. However, due to this behavior, the dialog title remains visible until the operation completes, making the user experience confusing. Ideally, the dialog should close immediately after the user interaction, regardless of subsequent operations.

Hey [USER], thanks for opening the issue! I agree that the flow in the example is not great.
For some background, right now we clean up stale nodes (e.g. the dialog after triggering st.rerun) after a `finished session` message. This means that the cleanup is only triggered _after_ the rerun is finished (here after the sleep), not when a new session / run starts.

I believe for handling this in a nicer way, we probably would need to expose the `close` function to the dialog so that you could manually indicate to the web app that you want to close it.
However, here is a (little bit hacky) way of doing this right now:

```python
def cb():
    st.markdown("<script>document.querySelector('[aria-label=\"Close\"]').click()</script>", unsafe_allow_html=True)

[USER].dialog("Cast your vote")
def vote(item):
    st.write(f"Why is {item} your favorite?")
    reason = st.text_input("Because...")
    if st.button("Submit", on_click=cb):
        st.session_state.vote = {"item": item, "reason": reason}
        st.session_state.dialog_closed = True
        st.rerun()
```

I have marke the issue as enhancement and not bug, because theoretically this is expected behavior in the current Streamlit execution model. cc [USER]

In my case, at version 1.52.2, all mentioned approaches above did not work.

But this worked:

```python
import streamlit as st
import time

def set_dialog_invisible():
    """Set the dialog to invisible using JavaScript."""
    css = f"""
    <style>
        div[data-baseweb="modal"] {{
            display: none !important;
        }}
    </style>
    """
    st.markdown(css, unsafe_allow_html=True)

# Make sure this state exists
if "dialog_closed " not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.dialog_closed = False

# This dialog is not dismissable with the "X" (Close) button
[USER].dialog("My Dialog", dismissable=False)
def my_dialog()
    st.write("Click close button")
        if st.button("Close"):
            st.session_state.dialog_closed = True
            st.rerun()

if st.session_state.dialog_closed:
    # This makes sure, that the closed dialog will be invisable, while rerun() is running
    set_dialog_invisible()
    # Start a long task, after dialog was closed
    st.write("Long task started...")
    time.sleep(10)
    st.write("Finish!")
    # Reset state
    st.session_state.dialog_closed = False
else:
    my_dialog()

```

Workflow explained:
1. Open this page and the dialog will open instantly (since the session state `dialog_closed=False`)
2. Close the Dialog with the button (this will trigger the `st.rerun()` and set `dialog_closed=True`)
3. With the rerun the `dialog_closed` state will call `set_dialog_invisible()` and start a long task


The most important change are:
- `!important` for the style definition
- call `set_dialog_invisible()` in the rerun, and not before
